result.topic_en: Ramanujan defines Q_8(N), the number of representations of N as a sum of eight squares divided by 16, and gives its Lambert-series generating function, a comparison with σ_3(N), an associated Dirichlet series, explicit multiplicative formulas, and the maximum order of Q_8(N).
result.transcription:
74. Let $\left(1+2q+2q^4+2q^9+\cdots\right)^8$
$=1+16\left\{Q_8(1)q+Q_8(2)q^2+Q_8(3)q^3+\cdots\right\}$
Then, by means of Elliptic functions, we can show that
(396) $Q_8(1)q+Q_8(2)q^2+Q_8(3)q^3+\cdots$
$=\frac{1^3q}{1+q}+\frac{2^3q^2}{1-q^2}+\frac{3^3q^3}{1+q^3}+\frac{4^3q^4}{1-q^4}+\cdots$
But $\sigma_3(1)q+\sigma_3(2)q^2+\sigma_3(3)q^3+\cdots$
$=\frac{1^3q}{1-q}+\frac{2^3q^2}{1-q^2}+\frac{3^3q^3}{1-q^3}+\cdots$
It follows that
(397) $Q_8(N)\leq\sigma_3(N)$
for all values of N. It can also be shown from (396) that
(398) $(1-2^{1-s}+4^{2-s})\zeta(s)\zeta(s-3)=Q_8(1)q+Q_8(2)q^2+Q_8(3)q^3+\cdots$
Let $N=2^{a_2}.3^{a_3}.5^{a_5}\cdots p^{a_p}$,
where $a_n\geq0$. Then from (396) we can easily show that, if N is odd, then
(399) $Q_8(N)=N^3.\frac{1-2^{-3(a_2+1)}}{1-2^{-3}}\frac{1-3^{-3(a_3+1)}}{1-3^{-3}}\cdots\cdots\frac{1-p^{-3(a_p+1)}}{1-p^{-3}}$;
and if N is even then
(400) $Q_8(N)=N^3.\frac{1-15.2^{-3(a_2+1)}}{1-2^{-3}}.\frac{1-3^{-3(a_3+1)}}{1-3^{-3}}\cdots\cdots\frac{1-p^{-3(a_p+1)}}{1-p^{-3}}$.
Hence the maximum order of $Q_8(N)$ is
$\zeta(3)N^3e^{Li(\log N)^{-2}}+O\frac{(\log N)^{-5/2}}{\log\log N}$
$=\zeta(3)N^3\left\{1+Li(\log N)^{-2}+O\frac{(\log N)^{-5/2}}{\log\log N}\right\}$,
or more precisely
(401) $\zeta(3)N^3\left\{1+Li(\log N)^{-2}+\frac{6(2^{1/6}-1)(\log N)^{-5/2}}{5\log\log N}+\frac{S_3(\log N)}{\log\log N}+O\frac{(\log N)^{-5/2}}{(\log\log N)^2}\right\}$

methods.what: Definition of Q_8(N) via the eighth power of the theta function (sum of eight squares)
Lambert series for the generating function of Q_8(N), via elliptic functions
Explicit product formula for Q_8(N), N odd
Explicit product formula for Q_8(N), N even
Refined asymptotic for the maximum order of Q_8(N)
